author: Jarrod Castillo
title: Caitlin Clark lets frustration boil over and gets technical foul in heated moment with referee - NewsBreak
text:
By Jarrod Castillo ,
1 hours ago LOS ANGELES - Caitlin Clark couldn't contain her emotions as the Indiana Fever battled the Los Angeles Sparks.
In the first half, the Sparks had a simple game plan for Clark : Make sure there is a body on her and make her play through contact. As the first 20 minutes of action progressed, Clark appeared to get progressively irritated with how she was being played.
So much so that in the waning moments of the first half, she couldn't contain what she was feeling. Her outburst came as her head coach, Stephanie White, shared what the star's next progression would be.
• Caitlin Clark tabbed for shocking next move by Fever head coach Stephanie White
• 'Ragebait' Caitlin Clark view sparks debate among WNBA fans
As the second quarter came to an end, Clark approached a referee and had a number of words for the official. It was clear that her frustrations reached a boiling point as she angrily clapped her hands in front of the referee, leading to a technical foul being called after the buzzer.
Despite how tough Los Angeles was playing her, with multiple players coming at her whenever she had the ball, Clark seemed to get whatever she wanted inside the 3-point line as the Fever led the Sparks 48-34.
In 15 minutes of action, Clark scored 11 points on 5-of-10 shooting from the field with six assists and two rebounds. She also had two fouls in the first 20 minutes of action and missed all of her 3-point attempts, going 0-for-4.
That said, Clark's ability to get into the paint and finish among the trees shows how comfortable she is with that facet of her game. What's more, the star's ability to shine up close could be a precursor to what White wants Clark to do in the future.
"I think she has a lot of room for growth," White said to reporters when asked by Mirror U.S. Sports before the game. "Really managing the game. Managing where we get her teammates on the floor and how we get them looks. Managing the way to manipulate the defense to get what you want."
White continued: "I keep telling her that we're going to add a post-up game too because she's got really great size and she's got great touch around the rim.
"She can add that, and being a facilitator from that position on the floor is another area."

The Fever also are working to make the game easier for Clark by relieving the pressure she faces when bringing up the ball.
"The biggest thing we're challenging her on this year is to play in line to in line across the floor, White surmised. "In college, it was mostly lane line to lane line.
"Last year, we wanted this to be free throw line extended to free throw line extended, so we really want to move her around the floor a lot more, and we want to try to ease up the burden that she has bringing the ball down the floor 94 feet against pressure all game long."
It remains to be seen how effective the star will be it is clear her tenacity remains, even during stopapges in play.
